answer: In each dispute thread, an agent marketplace weights votes by tokens locked for 30 days, with each token counted only once, regardless of how many identities hold it. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents gives the same voting power as keeping them in one. Even at the zenith of a coordinated attack, fresh accounts offer no oasis of free influence: the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and losing its use elsewhere.
